
'''Konpira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社), also known as '''Kotohira Shrine''' (琴平神社), '''Koto Hira Shrine''' (事比羅神社), or '''Konpira Shrine''' (金比羅神社), is a Shinto shrine dedicated to the deity {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}} ([[Konpira Gongen]]) with its head shrine located in {{ill|Kotohira, Kagawa|arz|كوتوهيرا|ca|Kotohira|ceb|Kotohira Chō|de|Kotohira (Kagawa)|es|Kotohira (Kagawa)|fa|کوتوهیرا، کاگاوا|fr|Kotohira|id|Kotohira, Kagawa|it|Kotohira|ja|琴平町|ko|고토히라정|ms|Kotohira, Kagawa|pl|Kotohira|ru|Котохира|simple|Kotohira, Kagawa|sv|Kotohira|tl|Kotohira, Kagawa|tr|Kotohira|uk|Котохіра|ur|کوٹوہرا، کاگاوا|zh|琴平町|qid=Q1271483|lt=Kotohira}}, {{ill|Nakatado District, Kagawa|ca|Districte de Naka-Tado|ceb|Nakatado-gun|de|Nakatado-gun (Kagawa)|es|Distrito de Nakatado|fr|District de Nakatado|id|Distrik Nakatado, Kagawa|it|Distretto di Nakatado|ja|仲多度郡|ko|나카타도군|pl|Powiat Nakatado|uk|Повіт Накатадо|zh|仲多度郡|qid=Q1206155|lt=Nakatado District}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|qid=Q161454|lt=Kagawa Prefecture}}. It is a place of worship for the Konpira faith and has many branches across Japan. Some branches use the term "shrine" (神社), while others use "palace" (宮).

== Overview ==
During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the Konpira faith spread widely across Japan through the efforts of maritime traders and merchants as shipborne commerce became more common. Branch shrines were established in many locations. Following the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ca|Haibutsu kishaku|de|Haibutsu kishaku|es|Haibutsu kishaku|fa|هایبوتسو کیشاکو|fi|Haibutsu kishaku|fr|Haibutsu kishaku|id|Haibutsu kishaku|it|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|ko|폐불훼석|pl|Haibutsu-kishaku|pt|Haibutsu kishaku|th|ไฮบุตสึคิชากุ|zh|廢佛毀釋|qid=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} (abolition of Buddhism) during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, the syncretic Konpira Daigongen faith was dismantled. Konpira shrines became Shinto shrines dedicated to Ōmononushi no Kami as their primary deity. There are about 600 shrines nationwide that align with the head shrine, {{ill|Kotohira-gū|abstract|Q94760|az|Kotohira məbədi|de|Kotohira-gū|eu|Kotohira-gū|fr|Kotohira-gū|ja|金刀比羅宮|ko|고토히라궁|simple|Kotohira-gū|sl|Kotohira-gu|tr|Kotohira-gū|zh|金刀比羅宮|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohiragū}}, worshipping Ōmononushi no Kami. Notably, there are still {{ill|Konpira Gongen|es|Konpira Gongen|ja|金毘羅権現|simple|Kompira|zh|金毘羅權現|qid=Q167077|lt=Shrines venerating Konpira Daigongen}} that continue to enshrine Konpira Daigongen without changing the main deity.
